title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The current generation, continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming. Key model IDs as of mid-2025:

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4 |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Balanced |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Current default Sonnet |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Most capable; also powers Claude Code Fast mode |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision.

---

## Claude 5 Family (June–July 2026)

Anthropic moved away from the Haiku/Sonnet/Opus-only versioning pattern by introducing a fourth, top-of-stack tier and splitting it into two variants with different safety postures:

- **Claude Fable 5 / Claude Mythos 5** (announced June 9, 2026) — the same underlying "Mythos-class" model shipped as two products. **Fable 5** is generally available and ships with safety classifiers that can decline risky requests or reroute them to Claude Opus 4.8. **Mythos 5** has no such classifiers and is limited to vetted partners under "Project Glasswing." Both share a 1M-token context window, 128K max output, adaptive thinking (always on, raw thinking never returned), and support for effort levels, task budgets, memory, context editing, and compaction. Pricing: $10 / $50 per million input/output tokens.
- **Export-control suspension** — On June 12, 2026, just three days after launch, Anthropic suspended access to both Fable 5 and Mythos 5 to comply with U.S. Department of Commerce export controls. The controls were lifted June 30, and access was restored July 1, 2026.
- **Claude Sonnet 5** (June 30, 2026) — the mid-tier successor to the Sonnet 4.x line, replacing `claude-sonnet-4-6` as the default balanced model.
- **Claude Opus 5** (July 24, 2026) — repositioned Opus as a cheaper, faster alternative rather than the priciest tier: $5 / $25 per million tokens, half of Fable 5's price, with an unchanged Opus price point versus Opus 4.8. It has a 1M-token context window, 128K max output, and a May 2026 knowledge cutoff — the most recent of any Claude model at launch. Opus 5 more than doubled Opus 4.8's score on Frontier-Bench v0.1, came within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak CursorBench 3.2 score at half the per-task cost, and scored 3x the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3. It became the new default model on Claude Max and the strongest available on Claude Pro, and is also the default Opus model in Claude Code.

This generation also introduced **Haiku 4.5** (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) as the fastest/cheapest current-generation model, continuing to sit below Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 in the lineup.

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K tokens (stable since Claude 2.1)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus)
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems
